content.text:
The current scrapers run four generic goals in parallel, and that's the main thing to fix. I read `docs/SWARM.md`, `swarm/scraper.py`, `agents/scrape_erp.py` and the challenge page's website section. I haven't run anything against the sites, so everything below is design advice, not tested behaviour.

## Main problem with the current setup

- **ERP and mail can't run blind.** The brief says the ERP won't list its catalogue for empty or over-broad searches and caps results at 20. Mail search ANDs its words, so it needs the exact tender reference plus a topic. So `scrape_erp` can't know what to search for until the tender and spec have produced the required attributes. `scrape_mail` can't search until the tender reference is known.
- **Fix: two COLLECT waves.** Wave 1 is tender and spec in parallel, and both post their facts early. Wave 2 is ERP and mail, which start by `board.wait_for` on the tender reference and the requirement list. Mail can start as soon as the reference exists, since it doesn't need the spec.
- **One browse per question.** A single 40-step browse over a whole site will run out of steps or context. Run several short browses, each with one narrow goal, for example "find the approval for this tender" or "find the ERP material for requirement N". The ERP and spec work can be spread over the 4 browsers, but only one browse per browser at a time.

## Making the output reliable

1. **Pass the model a schema per `kind`.** Right now `data` is free-form. Give each kind a small field list, for example for `erp.material`: material number, bore, stroke, pressure, mounting, certification, status, and the unit text as shown. Add a `source` (URL plus page or tab) and a `raw` text snippet.
2. **Keep facts raw, parse in code.** The agent records strings as shown ("1.234,50", "KW 12", "12.03.26 CET"). Plain helper code then normalises decimals, dates and timezones. The analysers interpret. Don't ask the model to do arithmetic or date maths while scraping.
3. **Make the model record negatives and provenance.** For example "searched X, 0 hits", "this document is superseded by Y", "no current revision marker found". Analysers and the verifier need these to tell "doesn't exist" from "didn't look".
4. **Have the agent cite what it saw on the page** (the row or snippet), not what it inferred. A cheap Qwen verifier can then check the record against the cited text.
5. **Use a screenshot for the odd cases.** Qwen has vision, so use it for canvas-rendered content (the earlier "canvas reading" commit) and for iframes or viewers where text extraction returns nothing.

## Trap handling

I'd put these in each scraper's `hints` as general strategy, never as values.

| Site | Trap | Instruction to give the agent | Code support |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| tender-portal | Cookie wall, flaky error pages | Dismiss the banner first. On an error page, reload or retry before concluding anything. | A small retry helper on navigation. |
| tender-portal | Docs behind an expression of interest | Look for an "interest" or registration action when a document is locked. | None. |
| tender-portal | ZIPs and iframes | Open the frame's own URL. For a ZIP, list its contents before opening members. | A helper that downloads a ZIP and lists or extracts text. |
| tender-portal | Timezone on the deadline | Record the deadline exactly as shown, with its zone label. | Normalise the timezone in code. |
| tender-portal | Q&A withdrawals and overrides | Record every Q&A item with its number, date, affected position and "withdraws answer N" text. Do not resolve them. | `analyze_quantities` applies "latest wins" and drops withdrawn answers. |
| tender-portal | Q&A assigns keys | Record Konditionsgruppe, tariff, commitment and pool keys as separate fields. | None. |
| customer-portal | Oldest revision opens first | List all revisions with their status or current marker and date, then open the current one explicitly. Also record the revision list itself. | The verifier checks that the requirements came from the current revision. |
| customer-portal | Nested viewers, paged tables | Follow the page counter until the last page. Report the row count seen against the count the page states. | A pagination helper over a model-selected table (allowed). |
| customer-portal | Data sheets name a Kataloggruppe | Record the Kataloggruppe per requirement. | None. |
| erp | Transaction codes, F4 popup | Find the code from the site's own menu or help. Use the F4 popup with narrow filters. | None. |
| erp | Results capped at 20 | Search by bore plus stroke plus pressure. If you get exactly 20 hits, narrow further. | A "hit count equals cap" flag that triggers a re-query. |
| erp | Short session timeout | Re-login when bounced to the login page, then resume. | A re-login wrapper in `browse`. |
| erp | Inactive materials | Record the status code and its legend. | The analyser filters on active status. |
| erp | Price conditions with validity and quantity scales | Capture every scale row, with its valid-from and valid-to dates and currency. | The analyser picks by scenario date. |
| mail | Look-alike approvals for other tenders | Search with the exact tender reference plus a topic. Record the reference as it appears in each message. | The verifier does an exact-match check on the reference. |
| mail | Superseded approvals | Record sent date, sender and any "replaces" text. | "Newest valid wins" and ignoring future-dated records happen in the analyser. |
| mail | Archive folder, paging | Search the inbox and the archive, and page through both. | None. |
| mail | Authorised senders only | Record the full sender address. | A sender allowlist that the model builds from the brief. |
| mail | Signing TAN | Don't fetch it early. | Only the submit agent reads it, close to signing time. |

A cross-cutting point is that every scraper should record the full sender, dates and revision labels, because the verifier relies on them.

## Prompting and tuning

- **Prompts.** Give each scraper a short role, an output contract (kinds and fields), a stop rule, and one line of strategy per trap. The brief is already injected, so don't repeat it.
- **Steps.** Raise `max_steps` for the wave-2 scrapers, but split their goals so each stays short.
- **Models.** Use Qwen for navigation and extraction. Add a second, cheap "did you miss anything?" pass that lists what was found and asks what's still unchecked. Use a stronger model only for ambiguous judgments.
- **Record as you go.** Have the agent post evidence as it finds it, so a timeout leaves partial data on the board. The orchestrator cuts COLLECT at 180 s before expiry.
- **Test on saved boards.** Run the full swarm once, then iterate with `SWARM_ONLY` and `SWARM_BOARD_IN` on `.swarm/board.json`.
- **Check coverage.** After each scouting run, compare each scraper's record counts per kind against what a manual browse shows, and fix the hints where they differ.

## Fair-play lines

- **Not allowed:** a helper that crawls a site and assembles the evidence, fixed click paths, or any scenario value in prompts or tests.
- **Allowed:** the retry, ZIP, pagination and parsing helpers above, as long as the model chooses what to open.
- **Private dataset.** It has different layouts and names, so write hints as "look for X" rather than "click Y". Never hardcode the transaction codes or status codes you see in scouting.

## Suggested split for three people

1. **Tender and customer portal.** `scrape_tender` and `scrape_spec`. This is the largest part and feeds everything else: the tender reference, quantities, Q&A and requirements, plus the revision selection.
2. **ERP.** `scrape_erp`, including the re-login wrapper, narrow-search strategy and the price-condition capture.
3. **Mail, plus shared helpers.** `scrape_mail`, the evidence schema per `kind`, the normaliser for numbers, dates and timezones, and the wave-1/wave-2 sequencing in the orchestrator.

Each person owns one file in `agents/`, as the swarm guide intends. Person 3 changes `swarm/` by small PRs. The first step is one scouting run, so we see where Qwen actually gets stuck before tuning hints.

I can draft the evidence schemas and the two-wave sequencing next.
/compact

1	"""The blackboard: the one place agents share data. Evidence goes in with its source; results are named values.
2	
3	Everything is JSON-serialisable so a board can be dumped to `.swarm/` and replayed in local development.
4	Single event loop, so no locks; `wait_for` lets a downstream agent start as soon as upstream posts.
5	"""
6	import asyncio
7	import json
8	import time
9	from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
10	from pathlib import Path
11	
12	
13	@dataclass
14	class Evidence:
15	    kind: str            # label agreed between producer and consumer, e.g. "tender.position" (see docs/SWARM.md)
16	    site: str            # siteId the fact came from
17	    data: dict           # the extracted facts, as found (no interpretation)
18	    source: str = ""     # URL / document / mail subject: where exactly it was read
19	    author: str = ""     # agent name
20	    note: str = ""       # caveats: superseded? withdrawn? timezone? uncertain?
21	    ts: float = field(default_factory=time.time)
22	
23	
24	class Blackboard:
25	    def __init__(self):
26	        self.evidence: list[Evidence] = []
27	        self.results: dict = {}      # named outputs: "quantities", "materials", "prices", "bid", "answer", ...
28	        self.errors: list[dict] = []
29	        self._changed = asyncio.Condition()
30	
31	    async def post(self, item: Evidence) -> None:
32	        async with self._changed:
33	            self.evidence.append(item)
34	            self._changed.notify_all()
35	
36	    def query(self, kind: str | None = None, site: str | None = None, prefix: bool = False) -> list[Evidence]:
37	        def match(e: Evidence) -> bool:
38	            if kind is not None and not (e.kind.startswith(kind) if prefix else e.kind == kind):
39	                return False
40	            return site is None or e.site == site
41	        return [e for e in self.evidence if match(e)]
42	
43	    async def set(self, key: str, value) -> None:
44	        async with self._changed:
45	            self.results[key] = value
46	            self._changed.notify_all()
47	
48	    def get(self, key: str, default=None):
49	        return self.results.get(key, default)
50	
51	    async def wait_for(self, kind: str | None = None, key: str | None = None, timeout: float = 600):
52	        """Block until evidence of `kind` exists (returns the list) or result `key` is set (returns it)."""
53	        def ready():
54	            if key is not None and key in self.results:
55	                return self.results[key]
56	            if kind is not None and self.query(kind):
57	                return self.query(kind)
58	            return None
59	        async with self._changed:
60	            await asyncio.wait_for(self._changed.wait_for(lambda: ready() is not None), timeout)
61	        return ready()
62	
63	    def error(self, agent: str, message: str) -> None:
64	        self.errors.append({"agent": agent, "error": message, "ts": time.time()})
65	
66	    def to_json(self) -> dict:
67	        return {"evidence": [asdict(e) for e in self.evidence], "results": self.results, "errors": self.errors}
68	
69	    def dump(self, path: Path) -> None:
70	        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
71	        path.write_text(json.dumps(self.to_json(), ensure_ascii=False, indent=1, default=str), encoding="utf-8")
72	
73	    @classmethod
74	    def load(cls, path: Path) -> "Blackboard":
75	        raw = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
76	        board = cls()
77	        board.evidence = [Evidence(**e) for e in raw.get("evidence", [])]
78	        board.results = raw.get("results", {})
79	        board.errors = raw.get("errors", [])
80	        return board

1	"""Runs the registered agents phase by phase. Agents of one phase run concurrently; a failing agent never stops others.
2	
3	Time: non-SUBMIT phases are cut off when the useful time is gone (ctx.time_left() <= 0), then SUBMIT always runs.
4	Local dev: SWARM_ONLY=a,b runs only those agents; SWARM_BOARD_IN=.swarm/board.json preloads a saved board (ignored
5	in scored runs). The board is dumped to .swarm/board.json after every phase.
6	"""
7	import asyncio
8	import importlib
9	import logging
10	import os
11	import pkgutil
12	from pathlib import Path
13	
14	import agents as agents_pkg
15	from swarm.agent import REGISTRY, Agent, Phase
16	from swarm.blackboard import Blackboard
17	from swarm.browser_pool import BrowserPool
18	from swarm.context import Context
19	from swarm.llm import LLM
20	
21	log = logging.getLogger("swarm")
22	BOARD_DUMP = Path(".swarm/board.json")
23	
24	
25	def discover() -> list[type[Agent]]:
26	    """Import every module in agents/ so its @register decorators run."""
27	    for mod in pkgutil.iter_modules(agents_pkg.__path__):
28	        importlib.import_module(f"agents.{mod.name}")
29	    return list(REGISTRY)
30	
31	
32	def select(classes: list[type[Agent]], only: str | None) -> list[type[Agent]]:
33	    if not only:
34	        return classes
35	    wanted = {n.strip() for n in only.split(",") if n.strip()}
36	    return [c for c in classes if (c.name or c.__name__) in wanted or c.__name__ in wanted]
37	
38	
39	async def _run_agent(agent: Agent, deadline_bound: bool) -> None:
40	    try:
41	        budget = agent.ctx.time_left() if deadline_bound else agent.ctx.seconds_left() - 60
42	        await asyncio.wait_for(agent.run(), timeout=max(1.0, budget))
43	    except asyncio.TimeoutError:
44	        agent.ctx.board.error(agent.name, "timed out")
45	        log.warning("%s timed out", agent.name)
46	    except Exception as error:
47	        agent.ctx.board.error(agent.name, f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}")
48	        log.exception("%s failed", agent.name)
49	
50	
51	async def run_swarm(task: dict, playwright, scored: bool, env=os.environ):
52	    board = Blackboard()
53	    preload = env.get("SWARM_BOARD_IN")
54	    if preload and not scored:                       # never replay data in a scored run
55	        board = Blackboard.load(Path(preload))
56	    ctx = Context(task=task, board=board, llm=LLM(), pool=BrowserPool(playwright), scored=scored)
57	    classes = select(discover(), env.get("SWARM_ONLY"))
58	    log.info("agents: %s", [c.__name__ for c in classes])
59	    for phase in Phase:
60	        agents = [c(ctx) for c in classes if c.phase == phase]
61	        if not agents:
62	            continue
63	        bound = phase != Phase.SUBMIT
64	        if bound and ctx.time_left() <= 0:
65	            log.warning("skipping phase %s: out of time", phase.name)
66	            continue
67	        log.info("phase %s: %s (%.0fs left)", phase.name, [a.name for a in agents], ctx.seconds_left())
68	        await asyncio.gather(*(_run_agent(a, bound) for a in agents))
69	        if not scored:
70	            board.dump(BOARD_DUMP)
71	    log.info("model calls: %d tokens: %s errors: %d", ctx.llm.calls, ctx.llm.tokens, len(board.errors))
72	    return board.get("answer")

        for entry in self.task["access"]:
            if entry.get("siteId") == site_id:
                return entry
        raise KeyError(f"no site {site_id!r}; have {[s.get('siteId') for s in self.task['access']]}")

    @property

        return [s.get("siteId") for s in self.task["access"]]

    def seconds_left(self) -> float:
        return contract.seconds_left(self.task)

    def time_left(self) -> float:
        """Seconds of useful work left (run clock minus the submit margin)."""
        return self.seconds_left() - SUBMIT_MARGIN_S

import enum
import logging
from abc import ABC, abstractmethod


class Phase(enum.IntEnum):
    COLLECT = 1   # scrapers: read the sites, post Evidence
    ANALYZE = 2   # analyzers: turn evidence into structured facts (quantities, requirements, candidate materials...)
    VERIFY = 3    # verifiers: cross-check authority / dates / tender reference / superseded records
    COMPUTE = 4   # calculators: deterministic arithmetic, set results["bid"]
    SUBMIT = 5    # fills the configurator, signs; ALWAYS runs, with reserved time


REGISTRY: list[type["Agent"]] = []


def register(cls):
    REGISTRY.append(cls)
    return cls


class Agent(ABC):
    name: str = ""               # defaults to the class name
    phase: Phase = Phase.COLLECT
    browser: int | None = None   # index of the browser this agent drives (0-3), None = no browser

    def __init__(self, ctx):
        self.ctx = ctx
        self.name = self.name or type(self).__name__
        self.log = logging.getLogger(self.name)

    @abstractmethod
    async def run(self) -> None:
        """Read from `self.ctx.board`, do the work, write Evidence / results back. Raise on failure (it is logged;
        other agents carry on). Stop early when `self.ctx.time_left() <= 0`."""
=== agent.py
"""Your agent's entry point: agent.json runs `uv run --no-sync python agent.py`, in the sandbox and on your machine.

The kit only does the plumbing: run.py reads the run and submits an answer, browsers.py attaches to the run's
browsers, models.py calls the hosted Qwen and Clef. Everything else is yours to build, in `solve` below.
Docs: $API/docs/building-an-agent.md, $API/docs/run-contract.md, and the rules: $API/docs/fair-play.md
"""
import asyncio
import json
import logging
import sys

from playwright.async_api import async_playwright

import run as contract
from swarm.orchestrator import run_swarm


async def solve(task: dict, playwright, scored: bool) -> dict | None:
    """Runs the swarm (see docs/SWARM.md). Agents live in agents/; the orchestrator runs them phase by phase.

    For an "api" submission the swarm leaves the answer in board.results["answer"]; for a "site" submission the
    submit agent enters it on the website and the result is None.
    """
    return await run_swarm(task, playwright, scored)


async def main() -> int:
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(name)s %(message)s")
    task, token = contract.load_run()
    sites = ", ".join(f"{site.get('siteId')} {site.get('url')}" for site in task["access"])
    print(f"Run {task.get('run_id') or '(local: the scouting logins, nothing counts)'}; websites: {sites}; "
          f"answer via {task['submission']['kind']}", flush=True)
    async with async_playwright() as playwright:
        answer = await solve(task, playwright, scored=bool(token))
    if answer is None:
        print("No answer to submit: build your agent in solve() in agent.py", flush=True)
        return 0
    if not token:
        print("Your answer (locally nothing is submitted):", json.dumps(answer, ensure_ascii=False), flush=True)
        return 0
    status, body = contract.submit_answer(task, token, answer)
    print(f"Answer: HTTP {status} {body[:2000]}", flush=True)
    return 0 if status == 202 else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(asyncio.run(main()))

# MVP plan for the agent swarm

The framework's plumbing is fine for an MVP. What's missing is the dependencies between agents, the data contract and the browser hand-offs. I re-read the code (`swarm/*`, every `agents/*` stub, `docs/SWARM.md`) and the rules in `CLAUDE.md`, but not the live brief, because you stopped that call. Check the 29 rules in `task["brief"]` against this before you start coding.

## 1. What the run gives us

| Input | Contents | Who uses it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `task["brief"]` | The job and its 29 bid rules. Treat it as the authority and re-read it on every run. | Every analyzer and the calculator, which pass the relevant rule text into prompts |
| `task["access"]` | A `siteId`, URL and login for each site | Scrapers and the submitter |
| `task["submission"]` | `kind = site`: the bid is entered in the tender-portal configurator and signed with a TAN | Submitter |
| `task["answer_schema"]` | The answer fields: reference, decision, discount, positions (material, qty, unit price, lead time, plus optional breakdown) and total | Calculator and submitter |
| The clock | 20 minutes. A late answer scores 0. | Every agent, via `ctx.time_left()` |

The private dataset uses different site names, so hard-coding `site_id = "erp"` won't work there. **MVP fix:** add a `SiteRouter` that makes one model call at startup, maps each role (tender, spec, erp, mail) to a `siteId` from `access` plus the brief, and stores it in `results["sites"]`. `SiteScraper` then looks up its role in that map.

## 2. Priorities, set by the scoring

- **Tender reference:** mandatory. Without it the bid is ineligible. Record it first.
- **Signed submission:** without it we score nothing.
- **Positions:** 75 points. Per position the weights are material 20%, quantity 15%, base price 15%, then 10% each for surcharge, packaging, bonus, final unit price and lead time.

**In the MVP:**
- reference, decision, quantity (with Q&A overrides and withdrawals)
- exact material match, base price on the scenario date at the reached quantity scale
- approved discount, lead time
- a signed bid with omitted positions allowed

**After the MVP:**
- Konditionsgruppe logic, metal-index surcharge, packaging cartons
- setup and pool fees, delivery commitments, project bonus bands, FX conversion
- nominal stroke derived from reserves

The optional breakdown fields stay **blank** in the MVP; blank is allowed when we don't have an answer.

## 3. How agents communicate

Agents never call each other. Everything goes through the blackboard, in three channels:

1. **Evidence**, streamed via `record`. These are raw facts exactly as shown on the page, with `source`. Only scrapers write them.
2. **Results**, as named keys. These are interpreted values with a documented shape. Analyzers, the calculator and the submitter write them.
3. **Done flags.** When a scraper finishes it sets `done.<role>` (a small change to `SiteScraper.run`). Downstream agents call `wait_for(key="done.tender", timeout=…)` and then read all evidence of that kind.

We need explicit done flags because `wait_for(kind=…)` returns as soon as the *first* record appears, which is too early to act on.

Every wait has a timeout. When it expires, the agent continues with whatever data exists; a partial bid is better than none.

## 4. Pipeline, browser use and connection points

```
                 COLLECT                         ANALYZE                    VERIFY/COMPUTE       SUBMIT
b0  TenderScraper ──tender.meta → results["tender_ref"] (set immediately)
                  ──tender.position / clarification ─┐
b1  SpecScraper   ──spec.revision / requirement / amendment
b2  ErpCandidates (waits done.tender) ──erp.material (candidates)
b3  MailScraper   (waits tender_ref) ──mail.discount_approval
                                     QuantityAnalyzer  → quantities
                                     RequirementAnalyzer → requirements
                                     MaterialMatcher (code) → materials
b2                                   ErpPricer (waits materials) → erp.price_condition / stock
                                     DiscountAnalyzer  → discount
                                                                   Verifier → verification
                                                                   BidCalculator → bid
b0                                                                                  BidSubmitter
b3                                                                                  TanReader → tan
```

**Two dependencies decide this layout:**
- **ERP needs to know what to search for.** Its search only works when narrowed to 20 hits or fewer. So the ERP work is split in two:
  - **ErpCandidates (COLLECT):** after the tender is done, it searches each position on a broad attribute, such as bore plus pressure, and records *every attribute* of each candidate.
  - **ErpPricer (ANALYZE, same browser):** it fetches price conditions, stock and lead time only for the materials that were chosen.

  Exact matching happens in code. Because the candidates were found on a broad attribute, an amendment like a changed stroke doesn't force a new search.
- **Mail needs the exact tender reference**, because mail search ANDs its terms. The tender scraper therefore sets `results["tender_ref"]` the moment it sees the reference, and the mail scraper starts from it.

**Browser hand-offs (we have 4 browsers):**

| Browser | First use | Later use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| b0 | tender scraping | submitter |
| b1 | spec scraping | — |
| b2 | ERP candidates | ERP pricing |
| b3 | mail approvals | reading the TAN |

The TAN may only be sent after signing is requested, so the submitter reads it at signing time. Confirm this while scouting.

## 5. Data contract (agree on this first)

Field names are generic and contain no values. All `data` values are strings exactly as shown; a shared `swarm/normalize.py` turns them into Decimal amounts, timezone-aware dates and units.

| kind | `data` fields |
| --- | --- |
| `tender.meta` | reference, title, deadline (with its timezone text), scenario/price date if shown, buyer |
| `tender.position` | position id, description, quantity, unit, any attributes listed |
| `tender.clarification` | Q&A number, date, position(s) concerned, new value or assigned key (Konditionsgruppe, tariff, commitment, pool), "withdraws N" text, withdrawn flag |
| `spec.revision` | revision id, date, status/current marker, approval (Technikfreigabe) |
| `spec.requirement` | revision id, position, bore, stroke / usable travel, pressure, mounting, certification, Kataloggruppe |
| `spec.amendment` | source, scope (positions), attribute, new value |
| `erp.material` | material number, bore, stroke, pressure, mounting, certification, status (+ legend), search used |
| `erp.price_condition` | material, valid from/to, scale quantity, price, currency, per-unit, condition type |
| `erp.stock` | material, available qty, shared yes/no, production lead time |
| `mail.discount_approval` | full sender address, sent date, subject, tender reference as written, percent, conditions/thresholds, "replaces" text, folder |
| `mail.tan` | sender, date, reference, TAN |

**Results** (each owner documents the shape at the top of their file):

| Key | Shape |
| --- | --- |
| `sites` | `{role: siteId}` |
| `tender_ref` | `str` |
| `quantities` | `{pos: {qty, basis}}` |
| `requirements` | `{pos: {bore, nominal_stroke, pressure, mounting, certification, revision}}` |
| `materials` | `{pos: {material, candidates_considered} \| null}` |
| `discount` | `{percent, conditions, source}` |
| `verification` | `{issues: [...]}` |
| `bid` | answer-schema dict, plus `omitted: [pos]` |
| `tan` | `str` |

**Two rules for every scraper prompt:**
- Record negatives too, such as "searched X, 0 hits" or "revision 2 not current".
- Record the list of things too: all revisions and all approvals, not just the one picked. The verifier needs that list to check the choice.

## 6. What each agent does in the MVP

| Agent | Approach | Traps it handles |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TenderScraper | 2 browse passes: (1) meta + positions, (2) the full Q&A | Cookie wall, error-page retry, expression of interest, iframes/ZIPs, timezone recorded as shown |
| SpecScraper | List all revisions first, then open the one marked current, then page through to the last page and compare the row count with the count shown on the page | Oldest revision opens first, nested viewers, paged tables |
| ErpCandidates / ErpPricer | The model finds the transaction codes itself from the site's menu or help. If a search returns exactly 20 hits, narrow it. Log in again when the session drops. | Transaction codes, F4 popup, status codes, timeout |
| MailScraper | Search with the exact reference plus a topic, in the inbox *and* the archive, across every page | Look-alike, superseded and future-dated mails |
| QuantityAnalyzer | Code: tender qty, then the latest non-withdrawn clarification by date. The model is used only to map a clarification to its position. | Withdrawn answers |
| RequirementAnalyzer | The model applies scoped amendments to the current revision; code validates the result | Wrong revision |
| MaterialMatcher | Pure code: an *active* material that matches every attribute exactly. If none matches, the position is omitted, or the decision is "no bid" per the brief. | Inactive materials, near-miss attributes |
| DiscountAnalyzer | Code: authorised sender, exact reference, date not after the scenario date, newest wins; the model only interprets the conditions | Look-alikes, superseded mails |
| Verifier | Deterministic checks (reference equality, authority, dates, every position complete) plus one cheap model cross-check | — |
| BidCalculator | Pure Decimal arithmetic with half-up rounding once at the end, in unit-tested functions | — |
| BidSubmitter | Browse: enter positions one by one, saving as it goes, then request signing, wait for `tan`, sign and submit. **Fallback:** when `seconds_left < 240`, sign whatever is entered. | Saving isn't scored, only a signed submission is |

**Time budget (1200 s):**

| Stage | Until | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| COLLECT | about 480 s | — |
| ANALYZE (incl. ErpPricer) | about 780 s | — |
| VERIFY + COMPUTE | under 30 s | — |
| SUBMIT | the rest | starts by about 840 s |

The orchestrator currently only cuts at 180 s before the end, so it needs **per-agent `budget_s`**.

## 7. Fair-play checklist

- The model chooses every navigation target and search term, derived from the brief and the evidence.
- Helpers may only parse, normalise, page through a result set the model chose, validate, compute and fill forms.
- There must be **no scenario values anywhere**: not in prompts, hints, tests or defaults. Tests use invented data.
- Hints describe a strategy ("find the transaction code via the menu"), never a click path or code learned while scouting.
- There must be no comments addressed to the reviewer.

## 8. Split for three people, with milestones

| Person | Owns | First deliverable |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **A** | `scrape_tender`, `scrape_spec` (+ `analyze_quantities`, `analyze_requirements`) | `tender_ref`, all positions and full Q&A on the board; current revision with complete requirements |
| **B** | `scrape_erp` → ErpCandidates + ErpPricer, `analyze_materials` | Candidates for every position, prices and stock for the chosen materials |
| **C** | `scrape_mail`, the TAN reader, `analyze_discount`, plus the shared pieces: `SiteRouter`, done flags, `normalize.py`, per-agent budgets, the contract in `SWARM.md` | Correct approval, TAN path confirmed, shared PRs merged early |

Having each scraper's owner also write its analyzer keeps the contract friction low. The calculator and submitter can go to whoever finishes first, or to the rest of the team.

**Milestones:**
- **M0, about 1 h:** agree the contract (§5). Browse the sites manually with `atira scout`. Run the current generic swarm once and inspect `.swarm/board.json`.
- **M1:** each scraper reliably fills its kinds on the scouting data. After that, iterate on saved boards with `SWARM_ONLY` and `SWARM_BOARD_IN`.
- **M2:** end to end on a saved board, producing an answer JSON and a signed bid locally.
- **M3:** `atira test-run . --follow`, then check timing and cost with the `atira` MCP tools.
- **M4:** add the items cut from the MVP in §2, ordered by points.

I can write this into `docs/MVP_PLAN.md` and update the contract in `SWARM.md`. I can also start on person C's shared PRs (site router, done flags, `normalize.py`, budgets) so A and B have something to build on.
Execute the plan step by step. Deliver the MVP that makes the agents work towards the goal. Goal is the working MVP

"""Model access for agents: concurrency-limited, usage-counted, JSON-friendly. Qwen by default (hosted, free)."""
import asyncio
import json
import re

import models


def parse_json(text: str):
    """The first JSON object/array in a model reply (tolerates ``` fences and chatter)."""
    text = re.sub(r"^```(?:json)?|```$", "", text.strip(), flags=re.M).strip()
    for opener, closer in (("{", "}"), ("[", "]")):
        start, end = text.find(opener), text.rfind(closer)
        if start != -1 and end > start:
            try:
                return json.loads(text[start:end + 1])
            except ValueError:
                continue
    raise ValueError(f"no JSON in model reply: {text[:200]}")


class LLM:
    def __init__(self, max_concurrent: int = 24):
        self._sem = asyncio.Semaphore(max_concurrent)   # team limit is 32 concurrent Qwen calls
        self._client = None
        self.calls = 0
        self.tokens = {"prompt": 0, "completion": 0}

    @property
    def client(self):
        self._client = self._client or models.qwen()
        return self._client

    async def chat(self, messages: list[dict], *, tools: list[dict] | None = None, model: str = models.QWEN_MODEL,
                   **kwargs):
        """One chat completion; returns the message (`.content`, `.tool_calls`)."""
        args = dict(model=model, messages=messages, **kwargs)
        if tools:
            args["tools"] = tools
        async with self._sem:
            reply = await self.client.chat.completions.create(**args)
        self.calls += 1
        if reply.usage:
            self.tokens["prompt"] += reply.usage.prompt_tokens or 0
            self.tokens["completion"] += reply.usage.completion_tokens or 0
        return reply.choices[0].message

    async def ask(self, system: str, user: str, **kwargs) -> str:
        message = await self.chat([{"role": "system", "content": system}, {"role": "user", "content": user}], **kwargs)
        return message.content or ""

    async def ask_json(self, system: str, user: str, retries: int = 1, **kwargs):
        """Ask for JSON; re-ask once with the parse error if the reply is not valid."""
        messages = [{"role": "system", "content": system}, {"role": "user", "content": user}]
        for _ in range(retries + 1):
            reply = (await self.chat(messages, **kwargs)).content or ""
            try:
                return parse_json(reply)
            except ValueError as error:
                messages += [{"role": "assistant", "content": reply},
                             {"role": "user", "content": f"Invalid: {error}. Reply with valid JSON only."}]
        raise ValueError("model did not return valid JSON")
"""Browsers for agents. In a run: CDP browsers 1-4 from the sandbox (never launch your own). Locally: one Chromium."""
import browsers


class BrowserPool:
    def __init__(self, REDACTED):
        self._pw = REDACTED
        self._contexts: dict[int, object] = {}   # slot -> browser context

    async def context(self, index: int = 0):
        n = len(browsers.cdp_urls())
        slot = index % n if n else 0             # locally everything shares one Chromium
        if slot not in self._contexts:
            _, page = await browsers.connect(self._pw, slot)
            self._contexts[slot] = page.context
        return self._contexts[slot]

    async def new_page(self, index: int = 0):
        """A fresh tab in browser `index`; tabs are unlimited, browsers are not (max 4)."""
        return await (await self.context(index)).new_page()
"""Shared swarm infrastructure. Agents live in `agents/`; see docs/SWARM.md."""
from swarm.agent import Agent, Phase, register
from swarm.blackboard import Blackboard, Evidence
from swarm.context import Context

__all__ = ["Agent", "Phase", "register", "Blackboard", "Evidence", "Context"]

  "setup": ["uv", "sync"],
  "run": ["uv", "run", "--no-sync", "python", "agent.py"],
  "browsers": 4,
  "models": ["qwen"]

"""The run contract: read the run (the brief, the websites and their logins, where the answer goes), submit the answer.

In a test run or a scored run the platform sets CHALLENGE_API_URL and CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN. On your own machine there
is no run token: `eval "$(atira scout --env)"` exports the public scouting run as CHALLENGE_SCOUTING instead, and
nothing done with those logins counts. Docs: $API/docs/run-contract.md
"""
import json
import os
import time
from urllib.error import HTTPError, URLError
from urllib.request import Request, urlopen

USER_AGENT = "atira-starter-kit/3"  # the API's edge refuses Python's default urllib agent
LOAD_SCOUTING = 'eval "$(atira scout --env)"; in PowerShell: atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression'


def http(url: str, token: str | None = None, payload: dict | None = None, timeout: float = 30) -> tuple[int, str]:
    """GET (or POST `payload` as JSON) with the run token in x-api-key: the status and the body."""
    headers = {"Accept": "application/json", "User-Agent": USER_AGENT}
    if token:
        headers["x-api-key"] = token
    data = None
    if payload is not None:
        data = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False).encode()
        headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
    try:
        with urlopen(Request(url, data=data, headers=headers), timeout=timeout) as response:
            return response.status, response.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    except HTTPError as error:
        return error.code, error.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")


def load_run(env=os.environ) -> tuple[dict, str | None]:
    """The run and its token; locally, without a token, the scouting run that `atira scout --env` exported.

    The run has `brief` (the task and its rules, markdown), `access` (per website: `siteId`, `url`, `credentials`),
    `submission` (`kind` "api" or "site", and its `url`), `answer_schema`, `started_at` and `expires_at`.
    """
    token = env.get("CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN")
    if not token:
        if not env.get("CHALLENGE_SCOUTING"):
            raise SystemExit(f"No run token and no scouting logins. To develop locally: {LOAD_SCOUTING}")
        try:
            return json.loads(env["CHALLENGE_SCOUTING"]), None
        except ValueError:
            raise SystemExit(f"CHALLENGE_SCOUTING is not the JSON atira exports. Load it again: {LOAD_SCOUTING}")
    url = env["CHALLENGE_API_URL"].rstrip("/") + "/v1/runs/current"
    status, body = 0, ""
    for attempt in range(5):  # rides out a restart of the API
        try:
            status, body = http(url, token)
        except (URLError, OSError) as error:
            status, body = 0, str(error)
        if status == 200:
            return json.loads(body), token
        if status in (401, 403, 404):  # the run is over, or the token is wrong: no point in asking again
            break
        time.sleep(2 * (attempt + 1))
    raise SystemExit(f"Cannot read the run: HTTP {status} {body[:300]}")


def seconds_left(run: dict, now: float | None = None) -> float:
    """Seconds until the run's `expires_at` (epoch milliseconds); after that the answer is refused and the run scores
    0. Every part of the answer scores on its own, so submit your best answer about a minute before time runs out
    rather than keep searching."""
    expires_at = run.get("expires_at")
    if not expires_at:
        return float("inf")
    return expires_at / 1000 - (time.time() if now is None else now)


def submit_answer(run: dict, token: str | None, answer: dict) -> tuple[int, str]:
    """POST the answer to the run's "api" submission target. 202: accepted and final, the run ends. 400: the body
    lists the issues; nothing is recorded, fix the answer and send it again. A "site" submission is entered on that
    website instead, and the website confirms it with a receipt."""
    submission = run["submission"]
    if submission.get("kind") != "api":
        raise ValueError(f"This run takes its answer on the website {submission.get('url')}, not through the API")
    if not token:
        raise ValueError("No run to answer: locally there is no run token. Test it in a run: atira test-run .")
    return http(run.get("answer_url") or submission["url"], token, answer, timeout=60)
"""The free hosted models in short: one call each. Docs: $API/start#models and $API/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls

Qwen (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next): an OpenAI-compatible chat model with tool calls, images and a 256k context. Every run gets
QWEN_BASE_URL and QWEN_API_KEY; on your machine `atira scout --env` points them at `atira models proxy`, which you
keep running in another terminal.

Clef (Cloudflare Clef): a decision model. POST $CLEF_BASE_URL/v1/decide with a `state`, up to 4 `images` and your
`questions`: "choice" picks one of your options, "noul" gives the probability of yes, "score" rates on your scale.
CLEF_BASE_URL and CLEF_API_KEY are set only where the platform hosts Clef. A run waits only for the models listed in
agent.json "models" to warm up: list ["qwen", "clef"] if your agent relies on Clef.

Any other provider works with your own key, through the run's metering proxy: see the docs above.
"""
import os

import httpx  # comes with the OpenAI SDK
from openai import AsyncOpenAI

QWEN_MODEL = "qwen3.8-flash-next"


def qwen() -> AsyncOpenAI:
    """A client for the hosted Qwen; a cold model takes a while to answer its first call, hence the long timeout."""
    return AsyncOpenAI(base_url=os.environ["QWEN_BASE_URL"], api_key=os.environ["QWEN_API_KEY"], timeout=360)


async def ask_qwen(prompt: str) -> str:
    """One chat call: the reply's text."""
    reply = await qwen().chat.completions.create(model=QWEN_MODEL, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}])
    return reply.choices[0].message.content or ""


async def ask_clef(state, question: str) -> float:
    """One decision: how likely Clef finds the answer to a yes/no question about `state` (text or JSON) is yes."""
    body = {"state": state, "questions": {"q": {"type": "noul", "instructions": question}}}
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=120) as client:
        response = await client.post(os.environ["CLEF_BASE_URL"].rstrip("/") + "/v1/decide", json=body,
                                     headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['CLEF_API_KEY']}"})
    response.raise_for_status()
    return response.json()["answers"]["q"]["noul"]
"""The run's browsers: attach over CDP and get a page. Driving them is up to you.

In a run the sandbox starts the browsers (agent.json "browsers": 1 to 4, default 1) before the clock starts and sets
CDP_URL (browser 1) and CDP_URLS (all of them, as a JSON array). Use those: the sandbox stops browsers your agent
starts itself. On your own machine there is no CDP_URLS, so `connect` starts a local Chromium (once:
`uv run REDACTED install chromium`; HEADLESS=1 hides it). Docs: $API/docs/building-an-agent.md
"""
import json
import os


def cdp_urls(env=os.environ) -> list[str]:
    """Every browser of the run, in order; [] on your own machine."""
    try:
        urls = [url for url in json.loads(env.get("CDP_URLS") or "[]") if isinstance(url, str)]
    except ValueError:

    urls = cdp_urls()
    if urls:
        browser = await REDACTED.chromium.connect_over_cdp(urls[number])
        context = browser.contexts[0] if browser.contexts else await browser.new_context()
    else:
        browser = await REDACTED.chromium.launch(headless=os.environ.get("HEADLESS") == "1")
        context = await browser.new_context()
    page = context.pages[0] if context.pages else await context.new_page()

class BoardTests(unittest.IsolatedAsyncioTestCase):
    async def test_post_query_and_wait(self):
        board = Blackboard()
        waiter = asyncio.create_task(board.wait_for(kind="a.b", timeout=2))
        await asyncio.sleep(0)
        await board.post(Evidence("a.b", "erp", {"x": 1}, source="u"))
        self.assertEqual((await waiter)[0].data, {"x": 1})
        self.assertEqual(len(board.query("a", prefix=True)), 1)
        self.assertEqual(board.query("a.b", site="mail"), [])

    async def test_dump_and_load_round_trip(self):
        board = Blackboard()
        await board.post(Evidence("k", "erp", {"x": 1}))
        await board.set("r", [1])
        path = Path(__file__).parent / "_board.json"
        try:
            board.dump(path)
            again = Blackboard.load(path)
        finally:
            path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        self.assertEqual(again.evidence[0].data, {"x": 1})
        self.assertEqual(again.get("r"), [1])

    def test_garbage_raises(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            parse_json("no json here")


def make_agents(order):
    class Boom(Agent):
        phase = Phase.COLLECT
        async def run(self): raise RuntimeError("boom")

    class Collect(Agent):
        phase = Phase.COLLECT
        async def run(self):
            order.append("collect")
            await self.ctx.board.post(Evidence("k", "erp", {}))

    class Analyze(Agent):
        phase = Phase.ANALYZE
        async def run(self):
            order.append(f"analyze sees {len(self.ctx.board.query('k'))}")

    class Submit(Agent):
        phase = Phase.SUBMIT
        async def run(self):
            order.append("submit")
            await self.ctx.board.set("answer", {"ok": True})

    return [Submit, Analyze, Boom, Collect]


class Orchestration(unittest.IsolatedAsyncioTestCase):
    async def run_with(self, classes, task=TASK, env=None):
        with patch.object(orchestrator, "discover", lambda: classes):
            return await orchestrator.run_swarm(task, None, scored=True, env=env or {})

    async def test_phases_run_in_order_and_a_failure_does_not_stop_the_rest(self):
        order = []
        answer = await self.run_with(make_agents(order))
        self.assertEqual(order, ["collect", "analyze sees 1", "submit"])
        self.assertEqual(answer, {"ok": True})

    async def test_only_filter(self):
        order = []
        await self.run_with(make_agents(order), env={"SWARM_ONLY": "Collect,Submit"})
        self.assertEqual(order, ["collect", "submit"])

    async def test_out_of_time_skips_work_but_still_submits(self):
        order = []
        late = {**TASK, "expires_at": (time.time() + 100) * 1000}   # inside the submit margin
        answer = await self.run_with(make_agents(order), task=late)
        self.assertEqual(order, ["submit"])

98	## Bid rules
99	
100	The brief states these rules in full. Together they define exactly one correct answer.
101	
102	1. **Quantity:** The tender quantity, overridden by the latest clarification that changes that position.
103	2. **Requirement:** The position's requirement in the specification revision marked current.
104	3. **Material:** The active ERP material whose bore, stroke, pressure, mounting and certification match exactly. If a position has none, the answer is no bid.
105	4. **Unit price:** The price condition valid on the scenario date, at the highest quantity scale reached, minus the approved discount, rounded half-up to the cent.
106	5. **Discount:** The most recent approval from the sales director for this exact tender; otherwise 0 %.
107	6. **Lead time:** The from-stock lead time when stock covers the quantity, otherwise the production lead time.
108	7. **Total:** The sum of quantity times unit price, rounded half-up to the cent.
109	8. **Decision:** Bid, with one entry per tender position; no bid with no positions and a total of 0 when a material is missing.
110	9. **Partial submission:** Full credit requires every position, but the bid form lets you explicitly omit unfinished positions (Position auslassen / Teilpunkte). They receive no position points; completed positions retain their independent credit. Review lists the omitted position numbers. You must still sign and submit a bid; saving alone is not scored. A missing active material still calls for no_bid for full correctness; omission is a way to submit incomplete work, not a replacement decision rule.
111	10. **Finding records:** The specification/data sheet names a Kataloggruppe for each requirement. Search the ERP for that group, then compare candidate attributes. Empty or over-broad searches do not list the catalogue; narrow to at most 20 results. Mail search combines words with AND: use the tender reference plus a subject/topic. Read the appropriate inbox/archive results. Opened pages and selected result sets may be extracted by helpers. Sites and positions can be investigated in parallel; no shared request quota or mandatory site order applies.
112	11. **Agent requirement:** A language model must choose navigation targets, searches and relevant documents from observations at runtime and make the important decisions. Helpers may extract a selected page, parse a selected document, paginate a model-selected result set, calculate, validate, retry and fill forms. They must not autonomously discover and traverse the websites to assemble the complete task evidence before model-directed investigation. Multiple agents and parallel browser sessions are allowed.
113	12. **Commercial clauses:** A tender Q&A answer may assign a position to a Konditionsgruppe. Resolve that key in the latest Konditionsregeln message for the exact reference from kalkulation@ plus the bidder mailbox domain. Its prose determines whether discount applies to base only, base plus mass surcharge, or neither; setup fees are always excluded. A group overrides the default rule, even when two positions select the same material. The separately reported surcharge is always BEFORE any discount. Positions without a group use the default base-only rule. The order-level approved percentage and its threshold calculation do not change.
114	13. **Withdrawn answers:** A tender Q&A answer may withdraw (zurückziehen) an earlier answer by its number. Ignore the withdrawn answer's quantity change; the latest remaining change applies, otherwise the tender quantity.
115	14. **Scoped amendments:** After selecting the governing full specification revision, read the tender Q&A for technical amendments naming that revision and requirement. Apply only the named attributes; all others are inherited. The latest dated applicable amendment wins per attribute. Amendments to other revisions do not apply.
116	15. **Shared stock:** Sum final quantities of all positions selecting the same material. Stock must cover that entire sum for every such position to use stock delivery; otherwise all use production delivery. No partial stock allocation. Price scales remain per position, not per material sum.
117	16. **Conditional discount:** The latest exact-reference director approval may require a minimum undiscounted net order value. Compute that value from final quantities and valid per-position scale prices before any discount and excluding mass surcharges and setup fees, rounded half up to cents. The threshold is inclusive. If it fails, use 0 %, without falling back to older approvals. For no_bid a conditional approval yields 0 %.
118	17. **Units:** Tender and Q&A quantities use the position's stated unit. Convert Satz using the governing specification's pieces per set. Price scales, inventory, allocation weights and bid quantities all use final pieces. Carton rounding affects packaging cost only, never the bid quantity.
119	18. **Pricing breakdown:** Base_unit_price, surcharge_per_unit, packaging_per_unit and rebate_total are optional and earn independent credit. All monetary answers are net EUR. Base, surcharge and packaging are per piece; rebate_total is the credit for the whole position. Enter 0.00 for a known zero; blank means unanswered. Do not feed rounded per-piece breakdowns back into the final formula.
120	19. These calculation rules apply to both practice and private datasets. Missing calculation fields lose only their own points; signing an incomplete bid is supported.
121	20. **Technical derivation:** For a requirement marked nutzbarer Weg, apply its scoped amendments first, then add twice the per-end reserve from the revision-specific Technikfreigabe. Match the resulting nominal stroke to the ERP. Do not change the other attributes.
122	21. **Authority and time:** Resolve each key from the latest record no later than the scenario date, for the EXACT tender reference. Authorized subjects/senders (local part + bidder mailbox domain): Technikfreigabe/technik, Verpackungstarife/logistik, Terminfreigabe/logistik, Devisenfixing/finanzen, Rüstpools/kalkulation, Projektbonus/finanzen. A newer record replaces the older one; a failed quantity condition does not revive it. Unrelated references and future-dated records never apply.
123	22. **Currency:** The valid condition names its currency and FX key. Normalize its price unit, select the per-position quantity scale, then convert with EUR per currency unit and HALF_UP to cents. This converted base_unit_price is used in all subsequent calculations and approval thresholds.
124	23. **Packaging:** Q&A assigns the tariff key; ERP gives pieces per carton. Charge ceil(final pieces / carton size) cartons independently per position. Do not increase the bid quantity. Report packaging_per_unit in EUR, rounded HALF_UP; do not discount packaging.
125	24. **Delivery:** Q&A assigns a commitment key. Apply it only if its material matches and pooled final demand for that material is within its inclusive ceiling. Otherwise use shared-stock delivery. A commitment may differ by position even for the same material.
126	25. **Shared setup:** Q&A identifies pool members; ERP gives allocation mass (distinct from surcharge mass); the Rüstpools mail gives the one pool fee. Allocate by quantity × allocation mass using the cent-allocation rule in that mail. Add each allocation to that position's ordinary setup fee. Report surcharge_per_unit BEFORE discount, excluding packaging and bonus.
127	26. **Project bonus:** The finance mail gives marginal percentage bands. Compute the eligible undiscounted EUR goods total, apply each band only to its portion, round the aggregate credit HALF_UP to cents, then allocate proportionally to eligible line goods values using largest remainders in cents (ties: ascending position identifier). Report rebate_total as the allocated EUR CREDIT FOR THE ENTIRE POSITION, not per piece; enter zero for nonmembers. This bonus is independent of discount clauses.
128	27. **Final price:** Clause-discounted EUR base + clause-discounted mass surcharge + (ordinary setup + allocated shared setup + carton cost − allocated project bonus) / final piece quantity. Use unrounded per-piece components and round HALF_UP once at the end. Sum quantity × rounded final unit price for total_net. Rounded breakdown fields are reports, not inputs to that final formula.
129	28. **Metal indices:** Select the latest exact-reference Preisindizes message from kalkulation@ plus the bidder mailbox domain. If the code lists validity windows, use the rate whose inclusive window contains the scenario date, not the last rate listed.
130	29. **Scoring in bid cases:** Decision 5, reference 5, discount 5, positions 75 minus any additional checks, correct total 5, arithmetic consistency 5. When present, the withdrawn Q&A quantity and date-selected metal-index checks earn 5 points each. Within each equally weighted position: material 20%, quantity 15%, base price 15%, surcharge 10%, packaging 10%, project bonus 10%, final unit price 10%, delivery 10%. Each field is independent; optional breakdown fields can be blank. No-bid scoring is unchanged.

132	## How a run works
133	
134	Develop on your machine against the public websites with the scouting logins (`atira scout --env`), then test in the sandbox: `atira test-run` uploads your package, starts a test run and opens it live, or drop the package on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team). A test run lasts up to 2 hours on the public data and returns its score with the full breakdown. In the commands, `$ATIRA_TOKEN` holds your personal token (sign in with `atira login`, then `atira token`).
135	
136	1. **Start.** The run issues a token, the task brief and fresh logins for every website.
137	2. **Read.** Your agent reads the brief, the rules and the answer format from the API.
138	3. **Work the websites.** It works through the 4 websites in a real browser and gathers the facts.
139	4. **Submit.** It enters the bid in the tender portal's configurator and signs it with a TAN from the webmail.
140	5. **Scored.** The answer is checked against the one correct answer; quality, cost and time are recorded.
141	
142	### Develop locally

144	```sh
145	eval "$(atira scout --challenge rfq --env)"   # logins for the public websites
146	curl "$ATIRA_API/v1/challenges/rfq/scouting"   # the same, with the brief, as JSON
147	# run your agent on your machine, then once in the sandbox:
148	atira test-run ./my-agent --challenge rfq
149	```

151	`atira scout --env` exports the scouting logins as `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS` (the shape a run gets), each website's URL, and `CHALLENGE_SCOUTING`, the brief and the answer format. It also points the free hosted models at `atira models proxy` on your computer, so your agent needs no model key; another provider takes your own. Nothing done there counts. With these logins, an answer entered on the tender portal is acknowledged but never counts. In a run, your agent reads the same at `GET /v1/runs/current` with the run token as `x-api-key`, and hands in one valid answer of up to 65,536 bytes; a malformed one returns its problems while the clock keeps running.

316	## Scoring and ranking
317	
318	Every submission is measured on its run in the sandbox.
319	
320	- **Quality:** 0 to 100. Every field of the bid is compared with the one correct answer: tender reference, positions, materials, quantities, unit prices, lead times, discount and total, each position's base price and surcharge per piece, packaging, allocated project bonus, and whether the total adds up.
321	- **Eligibility:** The right tender reference; a wrong decision loses quality points but other correct fields keep their credit. A bid that is not eligible ranks after every eligible one.
322	- **Cost:** Every model call goes through the proxy and is priced per model. There is no budget: at equal quality, cost × time decides.
323	- **Time:** Wall-clock time from the start of the run until the answer is accepted. It weighs as much as cost: halving either halves cost × time.
324	
325	Order: Eligible first → Quality ↓ → Cost × time ↑.
326	
327	Eligible answers rank first, then higher quality. At equal quality, the lower product of cost and time wins, with cost counted as at least $0.01 and time as at least 1 s, so among free runs the faster one wins.

340	## Fair play
341	
342	Your agent has to find the answer itself.
343	
344	- Your system must work the answer out from the websites at run time, with a model doing the navigating and deciding. A coding agent reviews every package; hardcoded answers, fixed scripts and crawlers are rejected.
345	- Bring your own model key for Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Google, Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI, Together, Fireworks, kept as a team secret. Every call goes through the run's proxy and is metered at the published prices. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare Clef are ours, unlimited. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair. The sandbox reaches the platform and the websites, nothing else.
346	- At most 4 browsers run at a time: ask for up to 4 in agent.json ("browsers"), use tabs and browser contexts inside them freely, and don't start browsers of your own, headless ones included. The sandbox stops any other browser your agent starts.
347	- One submission in flight per team. Submit again once it has finished.

8	
9	1. Quantity: start with the original tender quantity. For each position, use the quantity in the latest dated clarification that changes that position, if any.
10	2. Requirement: use the requirement referenced by the position in the specification revision marked current. Superseded revisions do not apply.
11	3. Material: select an active ERP material whose bore, stroke, pressure, mounting and certification all exactly equal that requirement. Blocked materials do not qualify. If any position has no matching active material, submit no_bid.
12	4. Unit price: use the material's price condition valid on the scenario date, including both validity endpoints. Choose the scale with the highest minimum quantity no greater than the final quantity. Apply the approved discount to that scale price and round the resulting unit price half up to the nearest cent.
13	5. Discount: use the most recent message from the sales director (leitung@ followed by the bidder's mailbox domain) that approves a discount for this exact tender reference. Approvals for other references and messages from other senders do not apply. If there is no approval, use zero percent.
14	6. Lead time: use the delivery-from-stock lead time in weeks when stock covers the final quantity; otherwise use the production lead time in weeks.
15	7. Total: sum each final quantity multiplied by its rounded discounted unit price, then round the total net amount half up to the nearest cent.
16	8. Decision: submit bid with one entry per tender position, identified by its position number, and currency EUR. If any active matching material is missing, submit no_bid with no positions and a total of zero.
17	
18	
19	## Additional rules
20	
21	These refine rules 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and 7 above. Every submitted quantity is in pieces.
22	
23	- Partial submission: full credit requires every position, but the bid form lets you explicitly omit unfinished positions (Position auslassen / Teilpunkte). They receive no position points; completed positions retain their independent credit. Review lists the omitted position numbers. You must still sign and submit a bid; saving alone is not scored. A missing active material still calls for no_bid for full correctness; omission is a way to submit incomplete work, not a replacement decision rule.
24	- Finding records: the specification/data sheet names a Kataloggruppe for each requirement. Search the ERP for that group, then compare candidate attributes. Empty or over-broad searches do not list the catalogue; narrow to at most 20 results. Mail search combines words with AND: use the tender reference plus a subject/topic. Read the appropriate inbox/archive results. Opened pages and selected result sets may be extracted by helpers. Sites and positions can be investigated in parallel; no shared request quota or mandatory site order applies.
25	- Agent requirement: a language model must choose navigation targets, searches and relevant documents from observations at runtime and make the important decisions. Helpers may extract a selected page, parse a selected document, paginate a model-selected result set, calculate, validate, retry and fill forms. They must not autonomously discover and traverse the websites to assemble the complete task evidence before model-directed investigation. Multiple agents and parallel browser sessions are allowed.
26	- Commercial clauses: a tender Q&A answer may assign a position to a Konditionsgruppe. Resolve that key in the latest Konditionsregeln message for the exact reference from kalkulation@ plus the bidder mailbox domain. Its prose determines whether discount applies to base only, base plus mass surcharge, or neither; setup fees are always excluded. A group overrides the default rule, even when two positions select the same material. The separately reported surcharge is always BEFORE any discount. Positions without a group use the default base-only rule. The order-level approved percentage and its threshold calculation do not change.
27	- Withdrawn answers: a tender Q&A answer may withdraw (zurückziehen) an earlier answer by its number. Ignore the withdrawn answer's quantity change; the latest remaining change applies, otherwise the tender quantity.
28	- Scoped amendments: after selecting the governing full specification revision, read the tender Q&A for technical amendments naming that revision and requirement. Apply only the named attributes; all others are inherited. The latest dated applicable amendment wins per attribute. Amendments to other revisions do not apply.
29	- Shared stock: sum final quantities of all positions selecting the same material. Stock must cover that entire sum for every such position to use stock delivery; otherwise all use production delivery. No partial stock allocation. Price scales remain per position, not per material sum.
30	- Conditional discount: the latest exact-reference director approval may require a minimum undiscounted net order value. Compute that value from final quantities and valid per-position scale prices before any discount and excluding mass surcharges and setup fees, rounded half up to cents. The threshold is inclusive. If it fails, use 0 %, without falling back to older approvals. For no_bid a conditional approval yields 0 %.
31	- Units: tender and Q&A quantities use the position's stated unit. Convert Satz using the governing specification's pieces per set. Price scales, inventory, allocation weights and bid quantities all use final pieces. Carton rounding affects packaging cost only, never the bid quantity.
32	- Pricing breakdown: base_unit_price, surcharge_per_unit, packaging_per_unit and rebate_total are optional and earn independent credit. All monetary answers are net EUR. Base, surcharge and packaging are per piece; rebate_total is the credit for the whole position. Enter 0.00 for a known zero; blank means unanswered. Do not feed rounded per-piece breakdowns back into the final formula.
33	- These calculation rules apply to both practice and private datasets. Missing calculation fields lose only their own points; signing an incomplete bid is supported.
34	- Technical derivation: for a requirement marked nutzbarer Weg, apply its scoped amendments first, then add twice the per-end reserve from the revision-specific Technikfreigabe. Match the resulting nominal stroke to the ERP. Do not change the other attributes.
35	- Authority and time: resolve each key from the latest record no later than the scenario date, for the EXACT tender reference. Authorized subjects/senders (local part + bidder mailbox domain): Technikfreigabe/technik, Verpackungstarife/logistik, Terminfreigabe/logistik, Devisenfixing/finanzen, Rüstpools/kalkulation, Projektbonus/finanzen. A newer record replaces the older one; a failed quantity condition does not revive it. Unrelated references and future-dated records never apply.
36	- Currency: the valid condition names its currency and FX key. Normalize its price unit, select the per-position quantity scale, then convert with EUR per currency unit and HALF_UP to cents. This converted base_unit_price is used in all subsequent calculations and approval thresholds.
37	- Packaging: Q&A assigns the tariff key; ERP gives pieces per carton. Charge ceil(final pieces / carton size) cartons independently per position. Do not increase the bid quantity. Report packaging_per_unit in EUR, rounded HALF_UP; do not discount packaging.
38	- Delivery: Q&A assigns a commitment key. Apply it only if its material matches and pooled final demand for that material is within its inclusive ceiling. Otherwise use shared-stock delivery. A commitment may differ by position even for the same material.
39	- Shared setup: Q&A identifies pool members; ERP gives allocation mass (distinct from surcharge mass); the Rüstpools mail gives the one pool fee. Allocate by quantity × allocation mass using the cent-allocation rule in that mail. Add each allocation to that position's ordinary setup fee. Report surcharge_per_unit BEFORE discount, excluding packaging and bonus.
40	- Project bonus: the finance mail gives marginal percentage bands. Compute the eligible undiscounted EUR goods total, apply each band only to its portion, round the aggregate credit HALF_UP to cents, then allocate proportionally to eligible line goods values using largest remainders in cents (ties: ascending position identifier). Report rebate_total as the allocated EUR CREDIT FOR THE ENTIRE POSITION, not per piece; enter zero for nonmembers. This bonus is independent of discount clauses.
41	- Final price: clause-discounted EUR base + clause-discounted mass surcharge + (ordinary setup + allocated shared setup + carton cost − allocated project bonus) / final piece quantity. Use unrounded per-piece components and round HALF_UP once at the end. Sum quantity × rounded final unit price for total_net. Rounded breakdown fields are reports, not inputs to that final formula.
42	- Metal indices: select the latest exact-reference Preisindizes message from kalkulation@ plus the bidder mailbox domain. If the code lists validity windows, use the rate whose inclusive window contains the scenario date, not the last rate listed.
43	- Scoring in bid cases: decision 5, reference 5, discount 5, positions 75 minus any additional checks, correct total 5, arithmetic consistency 5. When present, the withdrawn Q&A quantity and date-selected metal-index checks earn 5 points each. Within each equally weighted position: material 20%, quantity 15%, base price 15%, surcharge 10%, packaging 10%, project bonus 10%, final unit price 10%, delivery 10%. 	async def evaluate(self, page_function: str, *args) -> str:
		"""Execute JavaScript in the target.

		Args:
			page_function: JavaScript code that MUST start with (...args) => format
			*args: Arguments to pass to the function

		Returns:
			String representation of the JavaScript execution result.
			Objects and arrays are JSON-stringified.
		"""
		session_id = await self._ensure_session()

		# Clean and fix common JavaScript string parsing issues
		page_function = self._fix_javascript_string(page_function)

		# Enforce arrow function format
		if not (page_function.startswith('(') and '=>' in page_function):
			raise ValueError(f'JavaScript code must start with (...args) => format. Got: {page_function[:50]}...')

		# Build the expression - call the arrow function with provided args
		if args:
			# Convert args to JSON representation for safe passing
			import json

			arg_strs = [json.dumps(arg) for arg in args]
			expression = f'({page_function})({", ".join(arg_strs)})'
		else:
			expression = f'({page_function})()'

		# Debug: log the actual expression being evaluated
		logger.debug(f'Evaluating JavaScript: {repr(expression)}')

		params: 'EvaluateParameters' = {'expression': expression, 'returnByValue': True, 'awaitPromise': True}
		result = await self._client.send.Runtime.evaluate(
			params,
			session_id=session_id,
		)
		# Import here to avoid circular import
		from browser_use.actor.page import Page as Target

		return Target(self, target_id)

	async def get_current_page(self) -> 'Page | None':
		"""Get the current page as an actor Page."""
		target_info = await self.get_current_target_info()

		if not target_info:
			return None

		from browser_use.actor.page import Page as Target

		return Target(self, target_info['targetId'])

	async def must_get_current_page(self) -> 'Page':
		"""Get the current page as an actor Page."""
		page = await self.get_current_page()
		if not page:
			raise RuntimeError('No current target found')

		return page

import asyncio, json, os, sys
sys.path.insert(0, r"C:\Users\crubs\Desktop\tum_hackathon\ehl-finale-template")
from playwright.async_api import async_playwright
from swarm.page_text import EXTRACT_JS, clean

A = {a["siteId"]: a for a in json.loads(os.environ["CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS"])}["erp"]
UNLOCK = """() => { const r=document.querySelector('input[type=range]'); if(!r) return 'nogate'; r.value=100;
 r.dispatchEvent(new Event('input',{bubbles:true})); const c=document.querySelector('input[type=checkbox]:not([name])');
 c.checked=true; c.dispatchEvent(new Event('change',{bubbles:true}));
 const v=document.querySelector('#erp-receipt').getAttribute('aria-label').split(': ')[1];
 document.querySelector('input[name=receipt]').value=v; document.querySelector('input[name=acknowledged]').checked=true;
 document.querySelector('form[action="/notice"]').submit(); return v }"""


async def main():
    async with async_playwright() as p:
        b = await p.chromium.launch(headless=True)
        page = await b.new_page()
        await page.goto(A["url"])
        await page.fill("input[name=username]", A["credentials"]["username"])
        await page.fill("input[name=password]", A["credentials"]["password"])
        await page.click("button[type=submit]")
        await page.wait_for_timeout(800)
        await page.get_by_text("Notwendige Cookies akzeptieren").click()
        await page.wait_for_timeout(800)
        for _ in range(4):
            await page.goto(A["url"] + "/")
            await page.wait_for_timeout(800)
            if "/notice" in page.url:
                print("gate:", await page.evaluate(UNLOCK))
                await page.wait_for_timeout(1200)
            if "Easy Access" in await page.title():
                break
        for path in sys.argv[1:]:
            await page.goto(A["url"] + path)
            await page.wait_for_timeout(1000)
            print(f"===== {page.url}\n{clean(await page.evaluate(EXTRACT_JS, {}))}\n", flush=True)
        await b.close()

asyncio.run(main())
